result.rationale: The High Risk direction is well supported: first-party payment data shows a clearly deteriorating buyer, with days-late lengthening 9 to 19 to 52 across successive notifications and combined outstanding of 3.24M breaching the 3.0M credit limit on the sole reporting policy. The arithmetic is correct (0.65 x 74.0 + 0.35 x 77.8 = 75.3). However, the band depends materially on the news leg: payment weighted alone is 48.1, which falls short of the High Risk cutoff, so the 27.2 points from ILL-003 are what carry the score across it, and that article is anonymously and second-hand sourced. The underwriter should also note that the actual past-due amount is USD 640,000, not the 3240000.0 shown in the notification's owed field.

concerns.issue: The band rests on this single article. Payment weighted alone is 48.1, short of the High Risk cutoff; the 27.2 weighted news contribution is what lifts the score to 75.3. That places unusual weight on an item whose publication is recorded only as 'Illustrative' and whose body attributes the claim to three unnamed suppliers speaking to an unnamed regional business paper. Severity 4 with base 80.0 is a strong input for uncorroborated, second-hand, anonymously sourced reporting. Recommend confirming the underlying report before the High Risk band is released.

Probable double-count of a single underlying event. The article attributes the supplier arrears to a large customer postponing acceptance of two production lines - plausibly the same liquidity event generating the overdue invoice under TCI-EX-2026-0001. The formula combines payment and news as independent inputs weighted 0.65 and 0.35, so one cash-flow event may be scored twice. Two symptoms of one cause warrant less escalation than two independent problems.

Misleading exposure figure in the notification record. The owed field reads 3240000.0, but the payment review clarifies the actual past-due amount is USD 640,000, with 2.6M not yet due. Read directly, the notification substantially overstates at-risk overdue exposure. This does not affect the score, which uses DPD only, but will mislead anyone reading the notification unaided.

Ambiguous as-of date for the 52 DPD input. The record is dated 2026-10-02 and the review also refers to 2026-10-02 as the due date, so it is unclear whether 52 DPD is measured at the record date or at a later observation. ILL-003 was published 2026-11-08 with age_days 15, implying a scoring date well after 2026-10-02. If 2026-10-02 is the observation date, the payment leg is a stale snapshot and current DPD exceeds 52, understating payment raw 74.0; if it is the due date, the figure is current. This should be resolved, since it determines whether the payment leg alone would reach the High Risk band.
